title: Opening the quote page
intro: This covers everything from tapping a stock to a fully drawn quote page. Today the page makes about 18 requests, about 16 of them one after another, waits on fixed timers, keeps the whole header in a shimmer although the arguments already name the stock, and throws away or repeats several calls. The changes run the calls in parallel, remove the waits and duplicates, paint the header at once and cache data that rarely changes, each behind a Remote Config switch.

measured.current: 1,313 ms (header and market depth at about 0.3 s)
2,459 ms (one case still skeleton at 6.4 s)
measured.expected: 500 ms or less, no endless skeleton
about 14 (repeat: about 4), at most 4 in series

changes.title: Add Remote Config switches for quote loading
changes.summary: Several changes below alter loading order or show data sooner. Add one small flag holder in mo_get_quote, set from Remote Config by the app shell, so each change can ship dark and be rolled back without a release.
changes.risk_reason: Adds new code only. Every flag reads false when the Remote Config key is unset or unreadable, which keeps today's code path.

files.change: New static holder of bool Function() hooks, one per change (parallelOpen, progressiveOverview, sectionCache, keepTabData, keepTabsAlive, ...), all defaulting to () => false.
Reads FirebaseRemoteConfig.getBool for each key inside try/catch and wires the hooks, same pattern as ChartLibraryPrefetch.
Call QuotePerfFlagsInstall.install() next to ChartLibraryPrefetch.install().

changes.current: mo_get_quote does not depend on firebase_remote_config and has no feature flags. The app shell already uses a hook pattern for this: ChartLibraryPrefetch.install() (apps/super_app/lib/Common/chart_library_prefetch.dart) sets static callbacks in a package from Remote Config at startup.
steps: Create QuotePerfFlags in mo_get_quote with static bool Function() fields, each defaulting to () => false.

Create QuotePerfFlagsInstall in apps/super_app/lib/Common/ that maps Remote Config keys (quote_parallel_open, quote_progressive_overview, quote_section_cache, quote_keep_tab_data, quote_keep_tabs_alive, quote_keep_transactions, quote_header_from_args) to those hooks; any read failure returns false.
Call install() in app_initializer.dart right after ChartLibraryPrefetch.install() (line 945).
Read the flag at the start of each operation (open, tab switch), never inside build(), so one operation never mixes old and new paths.
safety: All keys unset means every change below stays on today's code path.
Same install pattern as ChartLibraryPrefetch, already in production.
regression_checks: App start with Remote Config unreachable: quote page behaves exactly as today.
Toggle one key in pilot and confirm only that behaviour changes.
changes.after_improvement: Each later change can be enabled per environment and per percentage, and rolled back in minutes.

changes.title: Run the opening calls in parallel
changes.summary: The open waits for dashboard, then getQuote, then scrip details, one after another. Start all three at once from the scripId in the arguments, and use the speculative scrip details only when the dashboard confirms the same cash scrip.
changes.risk_reason: Changes the order of the cubit's core open flow (loadAssetTypeData and _loadCashData). The dashboard decides the asset type and may redirect to dashboardData.cashScrip, so a wrong reuse would show the wrong scrip. Needs the flag and a full regression of cash, ETF, index, futures and options opens.

files.change: loadAssetTypeData: start dashboard, getQuote and scrip details together with Future.wait when QuotePerfFlags.parallelOpen() is on.
_loadCashData: take the prefetched scrip details when _getCashScripId() equals the arguments scripId, else fetch as today.
_loadScripDetails: accept an optional already-started Future.

changes.current: loadAssetTypeData awaits _loadDashboardData() (line 237), then fetchGetQuote (240). Only after that does _loadAndEmitAssetData run _loadCashData, which awaits _loadScripDetails (387) and then updateSelectedScripId, which calls getQuote again (1269). Four network round trips happen in series before the header leaves the shimmer.
steps: In loadAssetTypeData, when the flag is on, start three futures at once: _loadDashboardData(), fetchGetQuote(args scripId) and _repository.fetchQuoteScripDetails(args scripId). Skip the scrip-details prefetch for index scrips (quoteInfo.isIndexScrip), which do not call it today.
Await dashboard and getQuote with Future.wait; keep the rest of the method unchanged.

Pass the scrip-details future to _loadCashData. If _getCashScripId() has the same scripCode and exchange as quoteInfo.scripId, await that future; otherwise ignore it and fetch for cashScripId exactly as today.
For futures and options keep today's path in this change; they already reload scrip details for the contract they pick.
Attach .catchError to the speculative future so an unused failure is not reported as unhandled.
safety: Behind QuotePerfFlags.parallelOpen(); off keeps the serial chain.
The prefetched scrip details are used only when the dashboard resolves to the same scripCode and exchange, so redirected opens (F&O symbol opened as cash, cashScrip differs) fetch exactly as today.
Same endpoints and same parameters; only the start time changes.

Open an F&O contract whose dashboard.cashScrip differs from the argument scripId: header must show the cash scrip as today.
Open an ETF (no subtabs), an index, a futures contract, a spread and an option.
Open with network off and on a slow network: same error screen as today.
changes.after_improvement: Three round trips start together, so time to header drops from about 4 serial calls to about 1 (roughly 600-900 ms saved on a first open with typical 150-250 ms calls).

changes.title: Reuse the first getQuote result
changes.summary: updateSelectedScripId calls getQuote again for the scrip that loadAssetTypeData has just fetched. Reuse that response when the scripId matches.
changes.risk_reason: updateSelectedScripId is called on every exchange, expiry and strike change; the reuse must apply only on the open and only for the same scripId, or flags like hasDerivatives and CAS could come from the wrong scrip.

The second call is on the critical path before MoGetQuoteScripIdChanged and before the content area leaves the shimmer.
steps: Add a private field (ScripId, ScripQuote?)? _firstQuote set in loadAssetTypeData after the first getQuote.
In updateSelectedScripId, if _firstQuote matches scripCode and exchange, use it and set _firstQuote = null; otherwise call fetchGetQuote as today.
Keep the rest of the method (CAS flag, hasDerivatives, broadcast symbol, emit) unchanged.

after_code.code:
(ScripId, ScripQuote?)? _firstQuote; // set once in loadAssetTypeData

final (ScripId, ScripQuote?)? first = _firstQuote;
_firstQuote = null; // one-shot: later scrip changes always fetch
final ScripQuote? scripQuote = (first != null &&
        first.$1.scripCode == scripId.scripCode &&
        first.$1.exchange == scripId.exchange)
    ? first.$2
    : await fetchGetQuote(
        scripId.scripCode.toString(),
        scripId.exchange.value.toString(),
        isFromSearch: quoteInfo?.isFromDeepLink ?? false,
      );

changes.title: Load Overview sections in parallel
changes.summary: Overview sections are fetched one by one in a for/await loop (8 requests in series for a cash stock) and the per-section emit is commented out, so nothing below Market Depth shows until all are done. Fetch them in parallel and emit each section as it arrives.
changes.risk_reason: Changes the cubit's Overview state flow and emit count; sections appear in arrival order, which the accordion and visibility tracker must tolerate. Needs the flag and a full Overview regression.
changes.product_decision: With parallel loading, Overview sections will appear as their data arrives (within a few hundred ms) rather than all at once after about 1 s. Is it acceptable that sections pop in, or should we hold the first paint until the first three sections are ready? Proposed: emit progressively, but at most one emit per frame.

void _applyOverviewSection(final String section, final QuoteOverviewResponse r) {
  overviewDataManager = switch (section) {
    'News' => overviewDataManager.copyWith(newsData: r.processedNewsItems),
    'AnalystRatingV2' => overviewDataManager.copyWith(
        analystRatingData: r.hasRatingData ? r.ratingV2 : null),
    'QuantScore' => overviewDataManager.copyWith(
        quantScoreData: r.hasQuantScoreData ? r.quantScore : null),
    'ResearchIdeas' => overviewDataManager.copyWith(
        researchIdeasData: r.researchIdeasList.isNotEmpty ? r.researchIdeasList : null),
    'CorpActions' => overviewDataManager.copyWith(
        corporateActionsData: r.hasCorpActionsData ? r.corpActions : null),
    'Returns' => overviewDataManager.copyWith(
        stockReturnsData: r.returns.entry.isNotEmpty ? r.returns : null),
    'MfHoldings' => overviewDataManager.copyWith(topMutualFundData: r.getTopMutualFunds()),
    'SimilarStocks' => overviewDataManager.copyWith(
        similarStocksData: r.hasSimilarStocksData ? r.similarStocks : null),
    _ => overviewDataManager,
  };
}

changes.title: Cache static quote sections between opens
changes.summary: Every open starts cold: the cubit is a factory, the repository keeps nothing, and DIO caching only works if the server sends cache headers. Add an in-memory QuoteSectionCache keyed by URL with per-endpoint TTLs, and use the existing forced-cache plus cacheCallBack path for data that changes rarely.
changes.risk_reason: Data may be up to one TTL old when shown; wrong TTLs could show stale research or holdings. Repository-only change inside the module, behind a flag.
changes.product_decision: May the quote page show cached company data (scrip details, research ideas, fundamentals, peer list, returns) from an earlier visit while it refreshes in the background? Proposed TTLs: scrip details and dashboard 5 min, Overview research/ratings/returns/peers 15 min, Fundamentals 6 h, holdings and getQuote never cached.
changes.be_request: Send Cache-Control (max-age) and ETag headers on Quote/Dashboard, QuoteScripDetails, QuoteOverview (static sections), QuoteFundamental and CompanyReport so the existing DIO cache (CachePolicy.request) can revalidate with 304 instead of resending the body.

changes.title: Never leave the open stuck on a skeleton
changes.summary: The load chain catches only Exception, so a RangeError or StateError leaves the state on Loading forever; every call also waits up to the 20 s DIO timeout in series. Catch everything at the load boundaries, fix the known Error sources, and give the Overview an overall deadline after which it shows what it has.
changes.risk_reason: Changes error paths: some cases that hang today will show the error screen or partial content instead. The happy path is unchanged.

files.change: Add a final catch (e, st) that reports to Sentry/Crashlytics and emits MoGetQuoteError, so the state never stays on MoGetQuoteLoading.
indexWhere returns -1, never null, so ?? 0 does nothing and expiries[-1] throws RangeError; clamp to 0 or return when -1.
expiries.firstWhere(orElse: .first) throws StateError on an empty list; return early when expiries is empty.
_formatYear: split(' ')[1] throws RangeError for a period without a space; guard length.
Overall Overview deadline (e.g. 3 s, from Remote Config, 0 = off): emit current data and stop isOverviewLoading; late sections still merge.

changes.current: One measured open (HDFC Bank) stayed on the skeleton for more than 6.4 s. Two possible causes, both need confirming on device: (1) a serial chain where each call can wait the 20 s connect/receive timeout (DIOApiService2.dart:97-98); (2) an Error escaping 'on Exception' clauses. Confirmed Error sources: expiries[selectedExpiryStrikeIndex] with -1 (lines 735-740 and 808-813), .first on an empty futures expiry list (568-571), split(' ')[1] (2764). None of them is on the cash path, so for HDFC Bank cause (1) is more likely.
steps: At the end of loadAssetTypeData and _loadAndEmitAssetData add catch (Object e, StackTrace st) { report(e, st); if (!isClosed) emit(MoGetQuoteError(ErrorException.somethingWentWrong())); }.
Fix the three Error sources listed above.
Add the Overview deadline: Future.any([Future.wait(sections), Future.delayed(deadline)]) then emit and clear isOverviewLoading; sections that land later call _scheduleOverviewEmit (C7).
Log open duration and which call was slowest when it exceeds 3 s (ActivityLogger) to confirm the root cause in the field.

Errors are reported, not swallowed, so real bugs stay visible.

changes.title: Ask backend for a quote bootstrap endpoint
changes.summary: Even in parallel, the open needs three separate round trips before the header is complete, and Overview needs many sections. Ask the backend for one call that returns dashboard, getQuote flags and scrip details, cache headers on static data, and smaller payloads.
changes.risk_reason: New endpoint alongside the old ones; the app uses it only behind a flag and falls back to the three calls.
changes.be_request: 1) New GET Quote/Bootstrap?scripCode=&exchange=&source= returning QuoteDashboardResponse, the ScripQuote flags used by the app (hasOptions, hasDerivatives, hasCash, casEnabled, isin, sipAvailable) and QuoteScripDetails for the resolved cash scrip, in one protobuf. 2) Confirm that QuoteOverview with several &sections= returns the sections that succeeded even if one fails, and how failures are signalled per section. 3) Cache-Control/ETag on static sections (see C10). 4) List the response fields of QuoteOverview, QuoteScripDetails and QuoteDashboard that the app does not read, so they can be dropped or made optional, toward about 30 KB per open.
